parsed.elsewhere_quote:
Therefore \(\Gamma=\delta\). Xiang has at most \(n=(n+1)-1\) cuts, so the
lower half of the refinement lemma gives \(D\ge\delta\) for every one of his
marking choices.
parsed.explanation: The cut points for consecutive lengths δ,2δ,...,2^nδ are the partial sums (2^j−1)δ, j=1..n, not 2^jδ; e.g. n=1 gives marks at δ=1/3, not 2δ=2/3. So the quoted sentence is literally false. But nothing downstream uses the mark coordinates: the lower bound uses only the interval lengths (9), their unique binary subset sums, Γ=δ, and the refinement lemma's lower half, all stated separately. The corrected positions are still distinct and interior, so L3.3 stands; only the parenthetical description needs the symbol change 2^j → (2^j−1).
